costLabel: Notional API-equivalent cost (decision support, not a bill)
question: Would Claude Enterprise cost less per month than staying on the current plan, once productivity lost to throttling is counted?
method: current = subscription + throttle idle hours × idleToLostHoursFactor × loadedHourlyCost; enterprise = seats × seat price + max(0, notional spend − seats × included usage) × overage multiplier + current throttle loss × (1 − recovery%); net benefit = current − enterprise (positive favours migrating). Run-rates are trailing 30/90 complete local days scaled to 30.4375 days.

assumptions.label: Enterprise seat price (low)
assumptions.description: Placeholder assumption, not a quote: lower bound of the Enterprise per-seat price.

assumptions.label: Enterprise seat price (high)
assumptions.description: Placeholder assumption, not a quote: upper bound of the Enterprise per-seat price.

assumptions.label: Enterprise seats
assumptions.description: Seats bought on Enterprise; defaults to the seats on the current subscription.

assumptions.label: Usage included per seat
assumptions.description: Notional API-equivalent usage covered by each seat before usage-based overage applies (0 = all usage is billed).

assumptions.label: Overage price multiplier
assumptions.description: Usage beyond the included allowance is billed at this multiple of the rate-card list price (1 = list, 0.8 = 20% discount).

assumptions.label: Loaded hourly cost
assumptions.description: Fully loaded cost of one developer hour, used to value productivity lost to throttling.

assumptions.label: Idle-to-lost-hours factor
assumptions.description: Share of throttle-idle session hours that become lost developer hours (people switch to other work while an agent waits).

assumptions.label: Throttle loss recovered on Enterprise (low)
assumptions.description: Share of current throttle loss that Enterprise limits would remove — pessimistic case.

assumptions.label: Throttle loss recovered on Enterprise (base)
assumptions.description: Share of current throttle loss that Enterprise limits would remove — base case.

assumptions.label: Throttle loss recovered on Enterprise (high)
assumptions.description: Share of current throttle loss that Enterprise limits would remove — optimistic case.

low.description: Least favourable to migrating: high seat price, the heavier of the 30/90-day usage run-rates, the lighter throttling run-rate, low throttle recovery.

base.description: Mid seat price, 30-day run-rates, base throttle recovery.

high.description: Most favourable to migrating: low seat price, the lighter usage run-rate, the heavier throttling run-rate, high throttle recovery.

caveats: Notional API-equivalent spend prices metered tokens at rate-card list prices; the current plan has no per-token bill.
Enterprise prices are assumptions, not quotes: override seatPriceLow, seatPriceHigh, includedUsagePerSeatUsd and overagePriceMultiplier with the vendor quote.
Throttle loss values session idle hours at the loaded hourly cost scaled by idleToLostHoursFactor; an agent waiting on a limit does not always idle a person.
No crossover or break-even figure is produced by design: read the low–high range and the sensitivity table together.
Only 14 of 30 days are metered: the 30-day run-rate is extrapolated from them.
Only 14 of 90 days are metered: the 90-day run-rate is extrapolated from them.
